newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish customs staff end go-slow blocking border.
newsitem.headline: Polish customs staff end go-slow blocking border.

text.p: Polish customs officials on Wednesday called off a go-slow protest which had caused vast queues at several border crossings, the officials' union and the Main Customs Office (GUC) said.
Both sides announced they had reached a deal on the dispute, which largely concerned methods of paying a bonus which makes up half of the officials' pay.

"As a result of the talks and agreements, the Federation of Trade Unions of Customs Administration Employees decided to halt their protest action from 1.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), March 19," the Customs Office said in a statement sent to journalists.
Union chief Andrzej Gajda also told Polish public radio that all key issues had been settled and the protest halted.
The union's chief demand was that bonuses should be guaranteed rather than discretionary and Gajda said the president of GUC had agreed to include the regular bonus in work contracts."
The protest, underway since Monday, involved meticulous checks of every second vehicle and goods consignment rather than one in 10 or fewer, as is usual.

It led to tail-backs stretching tens of kilometres (miles) at five crossings with Germany and the Czech Republic on Tuesday as enraged truck drivers added to the chaos by using their vehicles to block access to the border for passenger cars as well.
Polish radio reported that on Wednesday morning the badly-hit crossings at Olszyna and Swiecko on the German border and Cieszyn, on the border with the Czech Republic, were now unblocked.
